leads.candidate: Zomereik (Pedunculate Oak, Quercus robur) in front of Kasteel Groeneveld
leads.why_not_shipped: Still single-sourced, and 2026-08-09's full read of the monumentaltrees list page changes the picture: the page does NOT describe 19448 as a solitary tree. Its own words are 'Voor het kasteel staat een grote groep eiken met een omtrek van ongeveer 4 meter en een hoogte van circa 28 meter' (a large GROUP of oaks stands in front of the castle, average girth ~4m/~28m); 19448 (4.70m/27.40m) is simply the one specimen someone measured and catalogued within that group. The RCE's own Groeneveld park monument description (511772, monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/511772) independently corroborates a formal oak planting at the entrance: 'de oprijlaan is beplant met drie rijen eiken in driehoeksverband' (the driveway is planted with three rows of oak in triangular formation). So this reads as an avenue/formal grouping, not a singular collectible point, which is a BRIEF_RESEARCH.md hard limit question ('An avenue or a whole wood is blocked') independent of the second-source gap. Recommend a future pass either (a) confirm via a site photo whether one tree in the group is visually the clear standout with 'one obvious place to stand', or (b) move this to blocked as an avenue. Not delivered either way this pass.

notes_2026_08_09_second_source_hunt: Dispatched specifically to find a SECOND SOURCE for the 10 candidates above (owner's instruction: 'zoek zelf nog maar even een tweede bron'), using fresh angles not tried before: Delpher (via a real browser session, since the site is client-side rendered and curl gets an empty shell), the RCE/monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl official monument descriptions for both Cantonspark (511682) and Groeneveld park (511772), cantonspark.nl's Historie and Park-impressies pages in full, Stichting In Arcadië's 2018-2021 historical/valuation report on Cantonspark, IVN Eemland's Groeneveld page in full, two Staatsbosbeheer Kasteel Groeneveld pages, Utrecht University's own Botanic Gardens history page, Wikipedia NL for both Kasteel Groeneveld and Cantonspark, a Groei & Bloei walking-tour page, Op de Heuvelrug, and iNaturalist. Zero of the 10 candidates cleared the two-source bar this pass either. Two things worth recording so nobody repeats this:

STRUCTURAL DEAD END, useful for any future Netherlands pass: monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl's own explanatory text states that for 'aangelegde monumenten' (parks/gardens, so-called 'groene monumenten') the register description deliberately does NOT list individual plantings ('dit geldt vooral voor de beplanting... dan wordt die veel te lang'), and confirmed in practice: Cantonspark's official description (511682) names only 3 species as examples of an 'extensive botanical tree collection' (tulip tree, hazel, snowdrop tree, none of which are the 7 pinetum candidates), and Groeneveld's (511772) names oak avenues and two lindens only, no beech at all. RCE will not give per-specimen species confirmation for a designed landscape monument; stop trying it for that purpose.

Delpher (delpher.nl/nl/kranten) is real and searchable but needs an actual browser: curl and WebFetch both get an empty client-rendered shell. A live browser session searching 'Cantonspark pinetum' returns 9 digitised newspaper hits (1920-1989), including a 40th-anniversary feature (Trouw, 17-06-1960, 'CANTONSPARK TE BAARN JUBILEERT') read in full via its OCR-text panel; it confirms the 1905/1918/1920 history already published on brn_001/002 but names no individual pinetum specimen, only 'prachtige bomengroepen... een pinetum en boomgaard' in passing. None of the 9 hits name a species. A future pass with more time could try narrower Delpher queries per species (e.g. 'Cantonspark sassafras', 'Cantonspark iep') rather than 'pinetum', not yet tried.

iNaturalist has almost no coverage at either site: zero observations for Sassafras albidum, Ulmus laevis, Quercus castaneifolia, Abies veitchii, Acer velutinum or a second Metasequoia near Cantonspark's coordinates; exactly one casual-grade Taxodium distichum observation, 2019-08-13, at 52.20803,5.29900 (inside the park), CC-BY-NC, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/34028145. That is a real 'alive as of 2019' data point for the Bald Cypress specifically but on its own is thin (casual grade, one observer) and its NC licence would rule it out as a photo regardless; noted for a future pass rather than used as a second source this time.

The beech copse and the nail-studded larch (monumentaltrees 19447/19449/19451/19450 and 3423) got the same full-text treatment from IVN, Staatsbosbeheer, RCE and Wikipedia as the front oak and turned up nothing at all naming them, not even in passing. Genuinely stuck without a source neither this pass nor the previous one thought to check; a next attempt might try the estate's own printed wandelroute/poeziebosroute leaflet (referenced as unfound in the 2026-08-09 deepen pass notes below) or a physical site visit / reader photo rather than more web search.
